# pnv

> A Dart CLI that lets you commit your secrets. Values are AES-256-GCM encrypted in plain-text YAML
> that lives in the repo; only the symmetric key lives outside it. At build time pnv decrypts the
> YAML into `.env`, and from `.env` into a Dart class of `String/int/bool.fromEnvironment` constants
> or a `--dart-define` argument string.
>
> This file is for an AI agent operating in a repo that uses pnv, or being asked to set pnv up.
> `README.md` is the human-facing version; this one is longer because it also carries the edge cases
> and the footguns. Everything below was verified by reading `lib/` and by running the CLI against a
> real project, not by paraphrasing the README — where the two disagree, trust this file and fix the
> README.

pnv is a **dev-time tool**, not a runtime library. It exposes no public Dart API — `lib/` holds only
`lib/src/**` and `lib/utils/constants.dart`, with no library entrypoint, so `import 'package:pnv/pnv.dart'`
does not resolve. If you are asked to "use pnv in code", the answer is that you shell out to the
executable, or you consume the Dart file it generated.

---

## The model, in one pass

```
  pnv init --yes     ──►  .pnvrc + <storage>/<flavor>.key   the key. NEVER in the repo.
                                    │
  envs/app.local.yaml               │                   committed. secrets are ciphertext.
    api-key: SECRET;v1:<b64>   ◄────┤ pnv set app.api-key "value" --file ...
                                    │ pnv get / pnv show      read it back
                                    │ pnv verify              is this safe to publish?
                                    │ pnv rotate              change the key
                                    │
                                    ▼ pnv generate env
  dist/app.local.env                                    gitignored. plaintext.
    API_KEY="real-value"
                                    │
              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
              ▼ pnv generate dart                         ▼ pnv to-dart-define
  lib/envs/app.dart                              -DAPI_KEY=real-value ...
    static const apiKey =                        (feed to dart/flutter build)
      String.fromEnvironment('API_KEY');
```

**Reach for `pnv set` before `pnv encrypt`.** `encrypt` prints a token you then have to place
yourself; `set` writes it where it belongs. `encrypt`/`decrypt` remain for values not going into a
file.

A **flavor** is a named key plus the file-suffix convention that selects it. Flavor `local` owns
`<storage>/local.key` and claims every `*.local.yaml` / `*.local.env`. A flavor may declare
**aliases** — extra suffixes that resolve to the same key — so flavor `production` with alias `ci`
means `app.ci.yaml` decrypts with `production.key`.

---

## Install and invoke

```bash
dart pub global activate pnv          # then: pnv <command>
dart pub add pnv --dev                # then: dart run pnv <command>
```

The binary is `bin/pnv.dart`.

Two global flags are stripped in `main()` before argument parsing, so they work in any position:
`--loud` (verbose) and `--quiet`. No `--version`.

Exit code is `0` on success, `1` on any failure. **Trust the exit code**: as of 2.0.0 every command
that cannot do what was asked exits non-zero and says which input it could not handle. Errors go to
the logger, so `--quiet` silences them and they are captured like any other output.

### Non-interactive safety — read this before scripting pnv

Any confirmation prompt goes through `mason_logger`, which throws without a TTY:

```
Bad state: No terminal attached to stdout.
```

**Every command can run head-less**, given the right flag. The three that would otherwise prompt:

| Command | What makes it safe |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | `--yes` (plus `--storage` / `--flavor` to skip the questions) |
| `create flavor` | `--force`, when the name already exists |
| `delete flavor` | `--force` |

Everything else — `set`, `get`, `show`, `verify`, `rotate`, `import`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`,
`create key`, `generate env`, `generate dart`, `to-dart-define` — never prompts.

---

## `.pnvrc`

JSON despite the name. Located **next to `pubspec.yaml`** — pnv walks up from the cwd to find
`pubspec.yaml` and looks for `.pnvrc` in that directory; only if no `pubspec.yaml` exists anywhere
above does it walk up looking for `.pnvrc` directly. It is created/rewritten by `init`,
`create flavor`, and `delete flavor`.

```json
{
  "storage": "~/.my_project",
  "flavors": {
    "local": [],
    "production": ["prod", "ci"]
  }
}
```

- `storage` — directory holding `<flavor>.key` files. A leading `~` expands to `$HOME`
  (`%USERPROFILE%` on Windows). **Commit `.pnvrc`; never commit the storage directory.**
- `flavors` — map of flavor name → alias suffixes. Flavor names are validated against
  `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` when created.
- **Every flavor name and every alias must be globally unique across the map.** A duplicate makes
  `PnvConfig.fromJson` throw `Flavors have conflicts...` and *every* command that loads the config
  fails with exit 1 — including `encrypt`. If pnv suddenly refuses everything, check for a repeated
  alias first.

---

## Commands

Verified against `lib/src/commands/**` and by running each one.

### Key selection — shared by `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `generate env`

Every one of these accepts `--key/-k`, `--key-file/-f`, `--flavor`. Resolution order, first match
wins (`CrypticCommand.secretFor`):

1. `--key <base64>` — the key literal.
2. `--key-file <path>` — file contents, trimmed.
3. `--flavor <name>` — `<storage>/<name>.key`; if that file is absent, pnv searches `.pnvrc` for the
   flavor whose alias list contains `<name>` and uses *that* flavor's key file.

With none of the three: `Invalid argument(s): Missing key, key file, or flavor.` — except
`generate env --file`, which falls back to inferring the flavor from the filename (see below).

A key must be base64 and at least 12 bytes once decoded; anything else is refused by name
(`Key is too short: 3 bytes, minimum is 12`). A *wrong* — but well formed — key is only detectable
at decrypt time, and reports as `Failed to decrypt (<file> → <key>). The value is well formed, so
this is most likely the wrong key.` A corrupt `SECRET;` token reports as malformed instead, and
says so explicitly rather than blaming the key.

### `pnv init`

```
-s, --storage <dir>         where keys live; default ~/.<pubspec name>
-f, --flavor <name>         a flavor to create; repeatable
-y, --yes                   take defaults, never prompt (required without a TTY)
    --gitignore             add *.key and *.key.previous to .gitignore
```

With `--yes` it never prompts, so it works in CI and project templates:

```bash
pnv init --storage ~/.my_project --flavor local --flavor production --yes --gitignore
```

Idempotent: re-running adopts existing key files rather than replacing them, and `--gitignore`
recognises entries it wrote before. Warns if the storage directory is inside the project.

Without `--yes` it is interactive. Prompts for the storage directory (default `~/.<pubspec name>`), adopts any
`*.key` files already in that directory as flavors, offers to create key files for flavors listed in
`.pnvrc` that have none, then loops prompting for more flavors. Writes `.pnvrc`.

### `pnv set <key.path> <value> --file <file.yaml>`

```
-i, --file <file.yaml>      REQUIRED (aliases: --input)
    --stdin                 read the value from stdin instead of an argument
    --plain                 write it unencrypted
-k/-f/--flavor              key selection (above)
```

Encrypts `value` into the file at a dotted path, in place. This is the normal way to add a secret.

```bash
pnv set app.api-key "sk-live-abc" --file envs/app.local.yaml
pbpaste | pnv set app.api-key --file envs/app.local.yaml --stdin
```

- Edits go through `yaml_edit`: comments, key order and indentation elsewhere are untouched.
- Groups on the way to the key are created if missing, in block style. An empty file works too.
- With no key flags the flavor comes from the **file name**, as `generate env` does.
- A path that runs through a scalar (`app.name.oops` where `app.name` is a value) is refused, and
  nothing is written.

### `pnv get <key.path> --file <file.yaml>`

Prints one value, decrypted. A plain (unencrypted) value is printed as-is — plain config lives in
these files too. Naming a group rather than a value is an error.

### `pnv show <file.yaml>`

Prints the whole file with every secret replaced by its plaintext, preserving comments and layout.
Takes the path positionally (as well as via `--file`) because that is how git hands it over. A file
with no secrets is passed through unchanged, so it is safe as a blanket textconv driver:

```gitattributes
*.local.yaml diff=pnv
```
```ini
[diff "pnv"]
  textconv = pnv show
```

### `pnv verify [--directory <dir>] [--file <f>]`

The check that pnv's premise — "this file is safe to publish" — actually holds. Read-only; exits 1
if anything is wrong. With no arguments it walks the project from the pubspec directory, skipping
`.git`, `.dart_tool`, `build`, `node_modules` and friends, and ignoring `pubspec.yaml` itself.

Four checks:

1. every secret decrypts under the flavor its file name implies (the v1 key id turns a cross-flavor
   paste into a specific message rather than a guess);
2. a corrupt token is reported as corrupt, not as a key problem;
3. no value that **looks** like a secret is sitting in plaintext;
4. the key storage directory is not inside the project (needs a `pubspec.yaml` to anchor "the
   project" — skipped without one).

Check 3 fires on credential **shape** (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`/`ASIA`, `xox[baprs]-`,
Stripe keys, `AIza…`, JWTs, PEM private-key headers, URLs carrying a password) or on a **key name**
that promises a secret (`key`, `secret`, `token`, `password`, `credential`, `auth`, `private`,
`cert`, `salt`) holding a value of 8+ characters. It deliberately stays quiet for names that are
public by convention (`public-key`, `key-name`, `key-id`, `auth-url`), for obvious placeholders
(`change-me`, `<your-key>`, `${VAR}`, `your-…`), and for empty values.

The escape hatch is a trailing comment, reusing the same convention as `# int` type declarations:

```yaml
demo-token: sk-live-not-real # plaintext, used in the public demo
```

### `pnv rotate`

```
-i, --file <file.yaml>      one file (aliases: --input)
-d, --directory <dir>       every .yaml in a directory (aliases: --dir)
    --from <flavor>         the flavor the secrets use now; default: per file name
    --to <flavor>           an existing flavor to move to
    --new-key               mint a fresh key for --from instead
    --dry-run               report without writing
```

Exactly one of `--to` / `--new-key` is required; `--new-key` also requires `--from`.

```bash
pnv rotate --directory envs --from production --to production-2026
pnv rotate --directory envs --from production --new-key
```

- Everything is re-encrypted in memory first. A file half under the old key and half under the new
  is the one unrecoverable state here, so a batch containing one unreadable file writes nothing.
- `--new-key` copies the old key to `<flavor>.key.previous` (chmod 600 — it still opens every
  secret written before the rotation) and installs the new one **before** rewriting the files, so a
  crash mid-run leaves both halves readable.
- **No key is ever deleted.** Retiring one stays a separate `pnv delete flavor`.

### `pnv import <file.env> --output <file.yaml>`

```
-o, --output <file.yaml>    REQUIRED
    --only-secrets          encrypt only what looks like a secret
    --force                 overwrite an existing output file
-k/-f/--flavor              key selection; otherwise from the OUTPUT file name
```

Builds an encrypted YAML from an existing `.env`, for adopting pnv in a project that already has
one. Encrypts **everything** by default — over-encrypting is safe, under-encrypting leaks;
`--only-secrets` applies the same heuristics `verify` uses.

Keys stay flat and lowercased (`APP_RUN_TIME_KEY` ⇒ `app_run_time_key`) so they regenerate
identically. Un-flattening is not attempted on purpose: `RUN_TIME` could have been `run-time` or
`run_time`, and guessing wrong renames the variable the build depends on. Nest them by hand
afterwards if you want the structure.

### `pnv create key`

Prints a fresh key to stdout, newline-terminated, and does nothing else — no file, no config.
32 cryptographically random bytes (`Random.secure`), base64url-encoded → a 44-character string
(43 characters plus one `=` of padding).

Keys created before 2.0.0 are 12 bytes (96 bits) and still work: every key is hashed to a 32-byte
AES key with `SHA-256(base64decode(keyfile))`, so key length is the entropy of the secret, not the
size of the cipher key. Rotating an old key gets you the full 256 bits.

### `pnv create flavor --name <name> [--force]`

Writes `<storage>/<name>.key` with a fresh key and adds the flavor to `.pnvrc`. Prompts (⇒ dies
head-less) if the name is already in `.pnvrc`. With no `--name` it prompts for one.

`--force/-f` overwrites an existing flavor without prompting. Use it whenever there is no terminal;
without it, an existing name prompts and therefore throws head-less.

> **Overwriting a flavor destroys its key**, and with it every secret encrypted under that key.
> There is no undo.

### `pnv delete flavor [--name <n>]... [--force]`

Deletes the key file and the `.pnvrc` entry. `--name/-n` is repeatable. Without any `--name` it
presents a multi-select prompt of existing flavors. Without `--force/-f` it asks to confirm each one.
A name that is not a known flavor is refused with exit 1 and the list of known flavors.
Irreversible: the key is gone, and every secret encrypted with it is unreadable forever.

### `pnv encrypt <value>... [key selection]`

Aliases: `enc`, `e`, `encode`. Encrypts each positional argument and writes one `SECRET;...` line per
value to stdout. Quote your values; a value with no positionals throws
`No values to encrypt provided.`

```bash
pnv encrypt "my api key" --flavor local
pnv encrypt --key-file ~/.myapp/local.key "$(pbpaste)"
```

### `pnv decrypt <value>... [key selection]`

Aliases: `dec`, `d`, `decode`. One plaintext line per argument. The `SECRET;` prefix is optional to
strip — pass the token exactly as it appears in the YAML.

### `pnv generate env` — YAML ⇒ `.env`

```
-i, --file <file.yaml>      one input file (aliases: --input)
-d, --directory <dir>       every file in a directory (aliases: --dir)
-o, --output <dir>          output directory      (default: "outputs")
-k/-f/--flavor              key selection (above)
```

At least one of `--file` / `--directory` is required. Output file name is
`<input basename minus its last extension>.env` — `app.local.yaml` ⇒ `app.local.env`. The output
directory is created if missing and is *not* wiped.

Key selection per mode:

- **`--file` with no key flags** — pnv derives the flavor from the filename and looks it up. So
  `pnv generate env -i envs/app.local.yaml -o dist` just works when flavor `local` exists. If the
  inferred flavor has no key the error names it.
- **`--directory`** — with `--flavor`, only files whose filename-flavor is that flavor or one of its
  aliases are processed, all with that flavor's key. With no `--flavor`, **every** file is processed
  and each one's key is derived from its own filename — this is the "regenerate everything" mode.

A `--flavor` that is not in `.pnvrc` is refused with exit 1 and the list of known flavors. It is not
treated as "no filter" — before 2.0.0 it was, so a typo generated every environment on disk.

The whole batch is rendered before any file is written, so a run that fails part way leaves the
output directory untouched rather than half-populated.

Filename ⇒ flavor (`FileMixin.flavorFrom`): if the basename has no dot, it *is* the flavor
(`local.yaml` ⇒ `local`); otherwise the second-to-last extension is used
(`app.local.yaml` ⇒ `local`, `infra.staging.env` ⇒ `staging`).

`pnv generate-env` (hyphenated, top-level) is a hidden deprecated alias that prints a warning and
delegates here.

### `pnv generate dart` — `.env` ⇒ Dart class

```
-o, --output <dir>          REQUIRED
-i, --file <file.env>       one input (aliases: --input)
-d, --directory <dir>       input directory (aliases: --dir)
    --flavor <name>         filter --directory by flavor
-c, --class-name <Name>     override the class name; --file only
```

> **The output directory is deleted recursively before writing.** pnv refuses, with exit 1, if it
> holds anything pnv did not generate — ownership is checked by the
> `// dart format off` header every generated file starts with, so re-running over pnv's own output
> is fine and pointing `--output` at a source directory is not. Before 2.0.0 the only check was for
> a subdirectory, and loose source files were destroyed silently.

Output file is `<input basename minus extension>.dart` with the flavor segment stripped:
`app.local.env` ⇒ `app.dart`, class `App`. `--class-name` applies only with `--file`.

Precedence inside `run()` is `--file` → `--flavor` (requires `--directory`) → `--directory`, first
match wins and returns.

Every env key must survive `toCamelCase()` into a legal Dart identifier. A key starting with a
digit, a key that becomes a Dart keyword, and two keys colliding on one field name are each refused
with exit 1 naming the offending key — rather than emitting a `.dart` file that does not compile.

### `pnv to-dart-define <file.env>...`

```
-l, --per-line              one -Dkey=value per line instead of one joined string
```

Reads every file, concatenates the lines, and prints `-DKEY=VALUE` arguments on stdout for
`dart`/`flutter build --dart-define`. Values are split on the first `=` only, unquoted, unescaped,
and stripped of any trailing `# type` comment.

> **A value containing whitespace cannot survive `$(pnv to-dart-define .env)`.** The shell
> word-splits the *result* of a command substitution, and no quoting inside that result prevents it
> — this is a property of the shell, not something pnv can fix. pnv warns on stderr, naming the
> keys affected. Use `--per-line` when any value has a space in it:
>
> ```bash
> pnv to-dart-define --per-line .env | xargs flutter build apk
> ```

`pnv create-key` (hyphenated) is a hidden deprecated alias for `create key`.

---

## Formats

### The `SECRET;` token

```
v1  SECRET;v1: + base64( keyId[4] || iv[12] || ciphertext[n] || tag[16] )   ← written now
v0  SECRET;     + base64( tag[16]  || iv[12] || ciphertext[n] || tag[16] )   ← still read
```

**`SECRET;` is the prefix in every version, and that is load-bearing outside this package.** Real
consumers glob `SECRET;*` to decide whether a value needs decrypting, and
`grep -E '^\s*key:\s*SECRET;'` to find blobs inside a YAML file. The version marker therefore goes
*after* the prefix, never in front of it. It is unambiguous because the base64 alphabet contains no
`:`, so a v0 payload can never begin with `v1:`.

AES-256-GCM. The IV is 12 fresh random bytes per call, so encrypting the same plaintext twice gives
different tokens — expected, not a bug, and the reason `git diff` needs `pnv show` to be readable.

**Both versions decrypt**; only new secrets are written as v1. A version *byte* inside the payload
would not work — it would be indistinguishable from the auth tag that used to occupy that position.

`keyId` is the first 4 bytes of `SHA-256("pnv:key-id:v1" || keyBytes)`. The domain separator is
load-bearing: the AES key is `SHA-256(keyBytes)`, so deriving the id the same way would publish four
bytes of it in every committed secret. It is a label, not a security boundary — the auth tag is what
actually rejects a wrong key — and it lets pnv say *"encrypted with a different key"* instead of
guessing. A v0 token has no key id, so `matchesKey` returns null there rather than false.

v1 also dropped the duplicated tag: v0 wrote it once via `cipher.mac` and again because
PointyCastle's `process()` appends it. A secret is 12 bytes smaller.

Key derivation: `AES key = SHA-256(base64decode(<keyfile contents>))`. Constants in
`lib/utils/constants.dart`; parsing in `lib/src/crypto/secret_token.dart`.

### YAML ⇒ `.env` mapping

```yaml
base-url: http://localhost:3000
app-secret: SECRET;VDlYm6Y2f0wo...
port: 8080
debug: true
db:
  host: localhost
  nested:
    deep-key: deep-value
```

```dotenv
BASE_URL="http://localhost:3000"
APP_SECRET="s3cr3t-value"
PORT=8080
DEBUG=true
DB_HOST="localhost"
DB_NESTED_DEEP_KEY="deep-value"
```

- Nested keys are flattened with `_`, uppercased, and `-` becomes `_`.
- **String values are emitted with surrounding double quotes**; `int`, `double`, `bool` are not; a
  null value emits `KEY=` with nothing after it. Any other YAML type (a list, for instance) throws
  `Unsupported value type`. **Lists are not supported.**
- Only string values starting with `SECRET;` are decrypted. Everything else is copied verbatim, so
  non-secret config lives in the same file.
- **Values are escaped**: `\` ⇒ `\\`, `"` ⇒ `\"`, newline ⇒ `\n`, carriage return ⇒ `\r`. So a
  multi-line secret (a PEM key, a JSON blob) survives as one `.env` entry. Before 2.0.0 nothing was
  escaped, so a quote produced unparseable output and a newline truncated the value at the break.
- Nesting leaves no trace of its own in the output — the key prefix already carries the full path.
  Comment lines in a hand-edited `.env` are still skipped on read, so adding your own is safe. The
  only comment pnv *reads* is a trailing `# type` declaration.

### Forcing a type (`# int`, `# bool`, `# num`, `# string`)

A trailing YAML comment on a value is carried into the `.env` line and is read back by
`generate dart` as a type declaration. This is how you type a key that is empty in some environments:

```yaml
db:
  port: # int          ⇒  DB_PORT= # int  ⇒  static const dbPort = int.fromEnvironment('DB_PORT');
```

Recognised (case-insensitive): `int` and `num` ⇒ `int.fromEnvironment`, `bool` ⇒
`bool.fromEnvironment`, `string` ⇒ `String.fromEnvironment`. Anything else warns and falls through
to inference. Inference without a declaration: `int.tryParse` succeeds ⇒ int; exactly `true`/`false`
⇒ bool; **everything else ⇒ String, including decimals** — `1.5` becomes
`String.fromEnvironment`, because Dart has no `double.fromEnvironment`.

A `#` inside a double-quoted value is part of the value, not a type declaration, so a secret
containing one is safe. Comments are read from the YAML value node's own source span — before 2.0.0
they were found by scanning the block for a line *containing* `<key>:` with the last match winning,
so a nested `db.port: # int` typed an unrelated top-level `port:`.

### Generated Dart

```dart
// dart format off
// ignore_for_file: lines_longer_than_80_chars

class App {
  const App._();

  static const baseUrl = String.fromEnvironment('BASE_URL');
  static const dbPort = int.fromEnvironment('DB_PORT');
}
```

Keys become `camelCase` fields. These are `fromEnvironment` constants, so **the values are baked in
at compile time from `--dart-define`** — the generated file holds no secrets and is safe to commit.
The `.env` files are the plaintext, and those are what must be gitignored.

---

## Recipes

**Set up a project without prompts.**

```bash
pnv init --storage ~/.my_project --flavor local --flavor production --yes --gitignore
```

**Add a secret.**

```bash
pnv set app.api-key "the-new-value" --file envs/app.local.yaml
```

**Check it is safe to commit.**

```bash
pnv verify        # exits 1 on a plaintext secret, a wrong-flavor value or a committed key
```

**Adopt pnv in a project that already has a .env.**

```bash
pnv import .env --output envs/app.local.yaml
```

**Full build path.**

```bash
pnv generate env  --directory envs --output dist       --flavor production
pnv generate dart --directory dist --output lib/envs   --flavor production
pnv to-dart-define --per-line dist/app.production.env | xargs flutter build apk
```

`--per-line | xargs` rather than `$(...)` because command substitution word-splits any value
containing a space. Use `$(...)` only when you know every value is a single word.

**Rotate a key.**

```bash
pnv rotate --directory envs --from production --new-key --dry-run   # look first
pnv rotate --directory envs --from production --new-key
```

The old key is kept at `<flavor>.key.previous` and nothing is deleted for you.

**Onboard a teammate.** `.pnvrc` and the YAML are already in the repo; they need only the key file
copied into their `storage` directory out of band.

## What must never be committed

- `<storage>/*.key` — the keys. `.gitignore` should carry `*.key`.
- The `.env` output directory — plaintext.
- Safe to commit: `.pnvrc`, the encrypted `*.yaml`, and the generated `*.dart`.

## Source map

| Where to look | For |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/src/pnv_runner.dart` | the command table |
| `lib/src/commands/cryptic_command.dart` | key resolution shared by encrypt/decrypt/generate env |
| `lib/src/crypto/secret_token.dart` | the `SECRET;` wire format, versions and key ids |
| `lib/src/handlers/encrypt_handler.dart`, `.../decrypt_handler.dart` | the cipher itself |
| `lib/src/crypto/plaintext_detector.dart` | what `verify` considers a leaked secret |
| `lib/src/commands/secret_file_command.dart` | shared plumbing for file commands (`leaves`, key-for-file) |
| `lib/src/commands/set_command.dart` | in-place YAML editing, including creating missing groups |
| `lib/src/mixins/file_mixin.dart` | YAML⇒env, env⇒Dart, escaping, type inference, `flavorFromPath` |
| `lib/src/mixins/pnv_config_mixin.dart` | `.pnvrc` discovery and storage paths |
| `lib/src/models/pnv_config.dart` | config schema, alias resolution, conflict check |
| `lib/src/handlers/flavor_handler.dart` | flavor create/delete |
| `lib/src/crypto/key_permissions.dart` | why key files end up 0600 |
| `test/e2e/` | executable examples of every command |
| `test/e2e/bad_input_test.dart` | the failure paths, one test per historical bug |
